slides.headline: A disease that hit 3.5 million now has 14 cases
slides.subline: **Guinea worm** is close to becoming the second human disease ever wiped out.

slides.body: In **1986**, guinea worm disease infected an estimated [[3.5 million people]] a year across 21 countries in Africa and Asia, the Carter Center says.
In **2023**, just [[14 human cases]] were reported worldwide. That is a drop of more than 99.999%.
There is **no vaccine and no cure**. People caught it from drinking dirty water. Filters, clean water and [[village health workers]] did the job.
Only **smallpox** has been eradicated in humans so far. Guinea worm would be [[the second]]. A few cases still keep appearing in a handful of countries.
What simple fix do you wish the world would roll out next? Tell us below.
